bugs: Carrier `rates` are only checked with is_array and then returned as-is. A body like {"rates":{"a":"x"}} is served as estimated:false with the wrong shape (app/Services/CarrierClient.php:41)

Carrier 4xx responses other than 401/404 (e.g. 403, 400, 429) fall back silently and are never reported. A revoked key that comes back as 403 would go unnoticed (app/Services/CarrierClient.php:56-60). Probe confirmed: 403 gives 200 fallback with nothing reported
antipatterns: tests/Feature/ShippingQuoteTest.php:9 defines a global `const CARRIER_RATES` in the Pest file. It leaks into the global namespace and can collide across test files
tests/Feature/ShippingQuoteTest.php:56 builds the 'array' case as `1234&postcode[]=1`, which relies on PHP query-parsing override behaviour and is hard to read
app/Http/Requests/ShippingQuoteRequest.php:12 uses regex:/^\d{4}$/ where the built-in digits:4 says the same thing
app/Http/Requests/ShippingQuoteRequest.php:9 rules() has no return type docblock (minor)
strengths: Uses Http::retry(3, 0, when) with a named isTransient predicate, so only ConnectionException and 5xx are retried and 401/404 are not
Timeout budget is explicit: 3 × 1.5s total, under 5s, with no sleeps; the one comment says what must stay true
Reports exactly the 401, as specified, and has a test proving transient failures are not reported
handleFailure(): never with named `previous:` arguments is clean, modern PHP
FormRequest plus validated('postcode'); controller maps domain exceptions to responses in one place
Tests use Exceptions::fake()/assertReported and preventStrayRequests globally in Pest.php; covers 5xx recovery, timeouts, fallback config, 401, malformed body

bugs: A carrier rate item missing `service` or `price_cents` causes an uncaught 'Undefined array key' ErrorException, so checkout gets a 500 instead of the fallback (app/Services/CarrierClient.php:74-77). Probe confirmed the 500

Every carrier failure is reported, including ordinary 5xx/timeout exhaustion (app/Http/Controllers/ShippingQuoteController.php:25). On a flaky carrier this floods alerting and drowns the 401 signal the task asked for
antipatterns: app/Services/CarrierClient.php:30-63 hand-rolls a retry for-loop with a $last tracker instead of using PendingRequest::retry(), which the installed framework provides
app/Http/Controllers/ShippingQuoteController.php:15-17 validates inline with $request->validate(...)['postcode'] instead of a FormRequest
app/Http/Controllers/ShippingQuoteController.php:19-31 sets $estimated/$rates across try/catch branches; returning directly from each branch would be clearer
app/Services/CarrierClient.php:74 uses array_values(array_map(...)) where a collection map would read better
app/Services/CarrierClient.php:16 defines a CONNECT_TIMEOUT that the 1.5s total timeout already caps, so it adds nothing
strengths: Normalises carrier rates to the documented {service, price_cents} shape with casts
Explicit status mapping: 404 becomes UnknownPostcode with no retry; 401 is not retried; other 4xx are not retried; only 5xx and connection errors are retried
Budget is reasoned: 3 × 1.5s with no sleeps
Good test suite: preventStrayRequests, an extensive invalid-postcode dataset including array input, attempt counting for connection failures, a 401 report assertion, malformed body

bugs: UnknownPostcode is thrown out of the controller and rendered via render(), but it is still reported by the handler. Every unknown postcode, a normal user-input case, logs an error (app/Exceptions/UnknownPostcode.php). Probe confirmed it is reported

report($e) runs for every non-404 RequestException and every ConnectionException, including routine 5xx/timeout exhaustion (app/Services/CarrierClient.php:38,42). That makes alerting noisy rather than flagging the 401 specifically
Carrier `rates` are returned unvalidated beyond is_array. Probe: {"rates":{"a":"x",...}} is served as estimated:false with an object instead of a list (app/Services/CarrierClient.php:47-51)
antipatterns: app/Services/CarrierClient.php:28-31 uses retry(..., throw: false) followed by ->throw(), which is roundabout compared with the default throwing retry
app/Services/CarrierClient.php:33-45 duplicates report-and-wrap across two catch blocks
app/Http/Controllers/ShippingQuoteController.php:15 crams the call and the response into one long line
Splitting error mapping between a render() on UnknownPostcode and a try/catch in the controller for CarrierUnavailable is inconsistent
strengths: FormRequest using digits:4, the most idiomatic rule
Http::retry with a when-predicate limited to ConnectionException and 5xx, plus a short 100ms backoff, inside a documented 4.4s budget
Global Pest beforeEach with Http::preventStrayRequests and Sleep::fake; one test asserts the exact sleep sequence to prove the time budget
Uses Http::failedConnection()/pushFailedConnection() fakes, assertUnprocessable, and a broad invalid-postcode dataset
Exception names without a redundant suffix, and named `previous:` arguments

v.rationale: All three pass their suites (impl-2 15 tests, impl-3 22, impl-1 18) and meet the core contract: 4-digit validation, bearer auth, 404 → 422 with a message, at most 3 attempts, worst case under 5s, fallback on failure, and a 401 that is reported and not retried. Laravel is 13.40. impl-1 ranks first: it uses Http::retry with a named transient predicate, reports exactly the 401 as specified (and tests that transient failures are not reported), uses a FormRequest, and has the cleanest error mapping. Its weaknesses are small: carrier rates are passed through unvalidated, and other 4xx responses fall back silently. impl-3 is close behind, with the best validation (digits:4) and the nicest tests (Sleep::fake asserting the backoff sequence, failedConnection fakes). It loses ground because the probe showed every unknown postcode being reported via the rendered exception, it reports every transient failure, it uses a roundabout retry(throw:false)->throw(), and it passes rates through unvalidated. impl-2 ranks last. It hand-rolls the retry loop instead of using PendingRequest::retry, validates inline instead of with a FormRequest, and reports every failure. Its rate normalisation, the only one that enforces the shape, crashes with a 500 when a rate is missing a key (confirmed by probe). That breaks the requirement that checkout always gets an answer.
